# SPD-080 — A skill and a size probe so new and changed code keeps the spudlib module rules

## Brief
Eric's ask (2026-09-15, right after SPD-065 landed): now that bin/spud_ledger.py is a 191-line orchestrator over the 58-module bin/spudlib/ package, add a skill so that updates and new code keep the rules the split established, instead of the package drifting back toward one big module. He restated the size rule in the same breath: the line count is not a hard limit.

His three decisions for this ticket, taken in the session that created it:
1. Scope is the Spud home only. BadTakes gets nothing here; its own conventions from BAD-036 stay in its spikes and its CLAUDE.md files.
2. A skill plus a reporting-only check: a probe that lists application code past the look-again point and prints what it found, and never fails a build or the suite. The rule is a prompt to look again, not a gate, so nothing here may turn it into one.
3. The rule itself gets one line in CLAUDE.md (always loaded, so it is never missed) and the detail lives in the skill. Spud writes the CLAUDE.md lines himself at return, because CLAUDE.md is his; you write the skill and the probe.

The size rule as Eric states it: ~250 lines is the point at which a module is worth a second look, never a cap. A module may be as large as it needs to be, and the larger it gets the more it must justify itself; no cohesive function, class or region is ever cut to fit a number. Scope is application code only (Python here); stylesheets, HTML and test files are out. At the time of writing the package's largest module is bin/spudlib/projects/install.py at 348 lines and eleven modules sit over 250, each of them deliberate.

The skill must teach more than the number, because the size rule is the least of what a new module here has to honour. Derive the rest from the sources and state each one with the reason it exists, so a reader understands the constraint rather than obeying it:
- Real modules importing whole modules, which was Eric's decision 1 on the SPD-065 spike over a one-namespace design. What the import idiom actually is in the package, and why importing a name by value breaks the test suite's monkeypatching at the call site.
- The hook path's import set. Every Bash, Edit and Agent call runs the PreToolUse hook, so a hook imports only its own event's modules; render, import, the parser, project install, schedule and doctor stay off it. What a new module must do to stay off it, and how a change to a hook module is timed (tests/probes/hook_timing.py, within 1 ms of main).
- The loader and the interpreter: python3.14 -I -S, nothing on sys.path, the finder that answers only spudlib from beside the entry, the bytecode cached under the home's state directory, and the entry that refuses to run directly.
- Where a new module goes among the nine directories, and what belongs in each.
- The one guarded import cycle in the shell analysis, and that a second cycle is a smell, not a precedent.
- What tests/test_package.py already guards, so the skill points at it rather than repeating it.

Read first: docs/spikes/spd-065/spud-ledger.md (the approved design), docs/spikes/spd-065/review.md (Cherie's review, which names the gaps), bin/spud, bin/spud_ledger.py, the package tree, tests/test_package.py, tests/probes/hook_timing.py, and CLAUDE.md. The ticket SPD-065 note carries Eric's decisions and the outcome.

Deliverables:
- .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, a project skill in the Claude Code shape (name and description frontmatter, the description written so it triggers when a session is about to write or change code under bin/). One skill unless you find two genuinely distinct trigger moments, in which case two, and say why in your result.
- tests/probes/module_sizes.py, following tests/probes/hook_timing.py's shape: run by hand, prints what it found, exits 0 whatever it finds. It reports application code only and never counts tests, and it names both thresholds, the ~250 look-again point and the 1000-line refactor trigger that started BAD-036 and SPD-065, as report bands rather than as pass or fail. Say in its header that it is advisory.
- A test for the probe under tests/, if the probe has behaviour worth pinning (its file selection and its banding, most likely). Keep it inside the existing suite's idiom.

Done when: the skill reads as guidance a stranger to this package could follow, the probe runs clean on the current tree and prints an honest report, the full suite passes (python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests), and no bytecode is left under bin/ or tests/. Name in your result the exact CLAUDE.md lines you would add, so Spud writes them.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus, no children: the skill and the probe are small and coupled (the probe encodes the thresholds the skill states). No fable while the usage limit holds. Spud writes the CLAUDE.md lines himself at return, per Law 1.
